en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī for Bestowing Fearlessness upon All,

Spoken by the Buddha. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Purple-Robed Subject Shi Hu, et al., in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was traveling and arrived at the Āmra Grove in the kingdom of Magadha.
He was dwelling in the Śakra Cave on Mount Vaidehī.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, came to where the Buddha was and, approaching him, addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
"I have a fear, namely that of the asuras,
who come to harass and disturb me throughout the long night. The asuras are my enemies."
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will proclaim for me the Dharma-gate of protection.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Lord of Devas, I possess a dhāraṇī."
It is named "Bestower of All Fearlessness.
This dharma is well able to accomplish all tasks and can eliminate all illnesses.
Furthermore, it can restrain all animals and untie all bonds of enmity.
Should there be asuras, rākṣasas, bhūtas, or any other heterodox beings, [it shall subdue them].
Even those seized by all manner of evil spirits and ghosts—
namely, those possessed by the wicked,
or seized by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, or gandharvas.
The seizing by kinnaras, the seizing by pināyakas,
and the seizing by mātṛkā-spirits are all completely extinguished.
Furthermore, if there are those who suck away vital essence, [they too shall be eliminated].
Those who consume flower garlands and those who obstruct childbirth,
as well as those who consume impurities— all are completely dispelled.
Furthermore, if there should be any malarial fevers whatsoever, [they shall likewise be removed].
Furthermore, all diseases such as wind, bile, phlegm, and mucus will be completely dispelled.
All battles, disputes, litigations, and hostile armies shall be utterly destroyed.
I now recite this dhāraṇī for you to provide protection.

The dhāraṇī is as follows: Tadyathā (1) eṇi (2) meṇi (3) prameṇi (4) prameṇiri (5) uru (6) mūri (7) mū... (7) Tadyathā: eṇi meṇi prameṇi prameṇiri uru mūri mū. (1) *Tadyathā* is pronounced with a long vowel (*ā*) in the first syllable; the following terms are to be recited accordingly. (2) *Eṇi*: *e* is short, *ṇi* is nasalized.

(3) *Meṇi*: *me* is long, *ṇi* is nasalized. (4) *Prameṇi*: *pra* is short, *me* is long, *ṇi* is nasalized. (5) *Prameṇiri*: *pra* is short, *me* is long, *ṇi* is nasalized, followed by *ri*. (6) *Uru*: *u* is short, *ru* is long. (7) *Mūri*: *mū* is long, *ri* is short. (7) *Mū*: *mū* is long. (All subsequent syllables are to be recited in this manner.)

Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī that bestows all fearlessness.
If there is one who maintains and recites it...
One should empower a pure thread forty-one times and tie it upon the crown of the head;
or empower white mustard seeds or ox-gall.
Whichever method is employed, accomplishment will be attained.
Furthermore, if one empowers scented ointment once and applies it to one's own body parts,
one will be like a person clad in armor— valiant and fearless—
neither wounded by blades nor afflicted by poisons.
Furthermore, they shall not be afflicted by malarial fevers lasting for one day, two days, or even up to seven days;
nor shall they be consumed by fire or drowned in water.
One shall not be harmed by spells, nor by malevolent spirits or demons, nor afflicted by disease.
One shall not die an untimely or violent death among any such calamities.
Furthermore, this dhāraṇī is well able to accomplish all corresponding ritual activities.
All methods of accomplishment are entirely harmonized;
there is no rite for accomplishment that will not succeed.
One is able to suppress all rites performed by others.
Unbound by others, one is able to shatter heterodox illuminations and cause one’s own Dharma to proceed accordingly;
all demonic obstacles can be dispelled,
and all possessive hauntings can be entirely dissolved.
"If there be any who hold onto attachments that cannot be removed,
their heads shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, [spoke thus].
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they leaped for joy and departed after paying homage.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī for Bestowing Fearlessness upon All*.
